doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Playing with Joe Williams in a Buffalo snowstorm
summary: Joe Williams's band was stranded, so Jeannie led a pick-up eight-piece; her opening blues won the audience.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: What was it about Joe Williams in Buffalo? He came through all this snow, that big one.
We don’t know how he got there, it was one of those big Buffalo snows.

And Miles Davis was supposed to be there, and Joe Williams. He was there. They made it through because — Sarah Vaughan couldn’t make it. But Joe made it, but his band didn’t make it. So they called us to get an eight piece group together to play with Joe Williams. And he was very nice, but every time he’d see a lady piano player they’d go — like they’re in pain. And it really made me mad but I knew I could do whatever he wanted. He says, “Okay.” He put the music up there. And I started playing Blues in G, I’ll never forget it.

He says, “Go ahead and play.” He says, “You open it up.” I think he wanted to find out where I was at before he started. And so I started playing this big old baby grand, a Steinway, and the audience started going oooh. Then they started cheering. And he said, “Take another one, take another one.” He was smart, see? But I’ll never forget that. Then we played his show, bang-bang-bang-bang, right down like that.
Yeah, he had a good time. He said, “This is the best band ever — I want to take you guys on the road.”
That was a great experience. That was the first time I’d ever played for him.
Well he knows how to work the audience. And he knows how to take advantage of the musicians.
He really does, he does. © Fillius Jazz Archive -28-
Yeah, he was a dear. And such a sweet person. You know some people have attitudes when they get on the bandstand. But he was wonderful.
